problem_framing.reason: A1 restates the question as the objective and lists three obvious alternatives. It never separates the business objective from the suggested consumer-proposition solution. Its constraints are not in the case: 'No expansion of the existing product line or market reach' contradicts the question, and the 20,000-euro budget and 12-week timeframe are invented. The rubric caps a dimension with invented numbers at 1. The framing also misses a premise the dossier corrects: hach-aquachek-number-one, retrieved in A2, shows Hach already sells consumer pool and spa test strips.

causal_mechanism.reason: T1 in A3 names a benefit: testing-kit sales and improved water quality. Its behaviour-change logic is incoherent, because customers 'unaware of the quality issues' would not therefore buy kits, and part of the text is truncated ('water-t'). It does not trace a credible chain from consumer behaviour to value Hach captures. It also rests on a misreading of hach-distribution-consumers (see red flags).

The 20,000-euro test budget, the 12-week timeframe and the no-expansion constraint appear nowhere in the case or sources.

T1 treats hach-distribution-consumers as grounds for consumer demand for testing kits. That source is a company claim about utilities testing distribution-system samples in the field before water reaches consumers; it says nothing about consumers buying kits. A3 also calls this Hach's 'existing consumer proposition' while ignoring the actual consumer line in hach-aquachek-number-one.

A1 sets the constraint 'No expansion of the existing product line or market reach', which contradicts the case question about developing a consumer proposition beyond existing instruments. It is presented as a given without support.
